welcome.text: Let me show you around while you scroll.
When you're ready to play, the table is one click away, and I'll sit beside you for your very first hand.

prologue.text: Every good evening starts with a sound: tiles clicking on felt.
Here the table shuffles for you, then pushes up four fresh walls, ready for the first hand.

arrive.text: Rex, Hiro, Lucky and Amara are strong, thoughtful players, each with a style of their own, and I'll be at the table too.
Practise with us until you're sharp.
And when your friends are free, start a table and share the link.
You'll be playing together in seconds.

learn.text: In your first game I talk you through every tile and tell you why.
Then the Academy has short voiced lessons, a placement test and fresh drills every day.
And after every game, I'll show you what you did right, and what to do better.

play.text: This is the real game, on a 3D table you can turn and tilt.
Every discard is called out loud.
If you get stuck, JongBot will tell you what it would play and why.
Turn the hints off whenever you feel ready.

rounds.text: A full game travels all the way round the table: East, South, West and North.
The dealer's seat moves on, and the wind of the round changes what scores.
Play one round over coffee, or all four for the whole evening.

ritual.text: Every corner of the table has its own side table.
Once a hand you can pour a bowl of tea and pass it to another player.
The gold coins beside you rise and fall with your score, and the dice are rolled to break the wall.

minigames.text: When you'd like a game for one, the Mini-games are always open.
There are twelve of them, from Solitaire to Match-3, all in 3D on your own tiles, table and room.
Every win earns Jong Points for the Atelier, and the daily puzzle gives the whole club the same board.
None of them touch your rating.

variations.text: Mahjong changed as it travelled, so we play it thirty ways.
Hong Kong, Riichi, Taiwanese, American, and the Dubai club rules.
Each one has its own scoring, its own lesson and its own cheat sheet.

collect.text: Every tile set here is its own object, with its own back, calligraphy and even its own click on the felt.
Choose tiles, racks or rooms, and look at them one at a time.
You earn them with Jong Points, and none of them change the game or your rating.

details.text: Choose a cloth for the table, a frame for your portrait, an outfit for your player, and even the way your win is celebrated.
They all add style and flair to your play.

interlude.text: Take a walk through the rooms.
A majlis in Dubai, a parlour in Tokyo, a Hong Kong tea house and the Imperial hall.
Each one has its own light, chairs and sounds.

world-tour.text: Take your passport around the Mahjong world.
There are eighteen destinations, each with its own rules, lesson and challenges that earn stamps.
Win in Hong Kong, Tokyo or a Dubai club, and that city's signature room opens for you.

club.text: When you want stronger company, the Club is here.
Every variation keeps its own rating, from Bronze to Master.
Seasons last six weeks, each themed on a city, with a league, a reward track and the Season Finals.
You can also start a private club for your friends.

final.text: Your seat is set, and I'm waiting at the table.
It takes one click to sit down.

about.text: Chacklate Experiences makes games the way a good chocolatier makes chocolate: with patience, care, and the finest ingredients.
JongClub began with a simple wish: to bring the warmth of a real mahjong table online.
So they built a premium club, and asked me to be your host.
Thank you for spending the evening with us.

item-tiles-classic-ivory.text: Every great collection begins somewhere, and ours begins here.
Classic Ivory is hand-finished to a soft, warm glow, each glyph cut crisp and filled by hand, set against deep jade lacquer.
Timeless, and it never goes out of style.

item-tiles-jade.text: Imperial Jade is carved from mottled stone, every glyph brushed by hand and a cloud engraved into each back.
No two tiles carry quite the same markings.
It is a set people notice from across the room.

item-tiles-obsidian.text: This is one of my favourites.
Obsidian and Gold is polished volcanic glass, with glyphs laid in real gold leaf and kintsugi veins traced by hand across every back.
Dramatic, a little dangerous, and utterly unforgettable at the table.

item-tiles-pearl.text: Turn one slowly in the light.
Mother of Pearl is meticulously cut from iridescent shell, so every face shifts from rose to lilac as it moves, with scalloped backs to match.
It is the most romantic set in the atelier.

item-tiles-crystal.text: Ice Crystal is pure faceted glass, ground and polished by hand until the glyphs seem to glow from deep inside.
And listen when they touch: a bright, clear chime.
It turns every discard into a small moment.

item-tiles-black-marble.text: Carrara and Nero is stone at its noblest.
The faces are white Carrara, engraved like a monument, and each back is cut from veined black marble.
Heavy, cool to the touch, and built to outlast all of us.

item-tiles-royal-gold.text: For those who play to win, and want everyone to know it.
Imperial Gold is fully gilded, with hand-chased filigree corners and an embossed dragon seal on every single back.
It is the set that makes a statement before you play a tile.

item-tiles-champagne.text: Blush faces lettered in fine Song calligraphy, rose-gold backs etched with an Art Deco fan.
It is a set made for long evenings and something sparkling in the glass.

item-tiles-sapphire.text: This is a love letter to the Ming kilns.
Blue and White Porcelain is hand-painted in deep cobalt beneath a glassy glaze, and every back carries rolling waves drawn stroke by stroke.
Museum-worthy, and yours to play with.

item-tiles-emerald.text: Malachite and Gold is cut from banded green stone, so no two bodies share the same rings.
The white faces are framed in hand-laid gold.

item-tiles-cinnabar.text: Cinnabar was once reserved for the imperial court.
These faces are carved in layer upon layer of red lacquer, the brushwork picked out in gold, on deep black bodies.

item-tiles-walnut.text: Some people like their tiles warm and honest.
Walnut and Brass is hand-oiled wood, inlaid with bone and polished brass, and it makes the most satisfying hollow click.
It ages beautifully, like a good leather chair.

item-tiles-noyer.text: Ah, the masterpiece of the house.
Noyer and Ivoire fuses ivory faces to solid walnut, and every back is stamped with a gilt sparrow seal by hand.
It is the set our most devoted members save for.

item-tiles-amethyst.text: Polished amethyst set in a gold bezel, gilt symbols, and a ruby cabochon set into every face.
Play a hand with these and you are wearing the crown.

item-tiles-gilt-porcelain.text: Gilded Porcelain is delicate, but never fragile.
Fine white porcelain framed in beaded gilt, on blush backs with a layered resin edge you can feel under your thumb.

item-tiles-bone-bamboo.text: These are made the old way.
Bone and Bamboo pairs hand-carved bone faces dovetailed into bamboo backs, just as the great masters did a century ago.
For the player who respects where this game comes from.

item-tiles-season-hongkong.text: Harbour Lights is something money cannot buy.
This set belongs to the Hong Kong season alone, earned on the reward track by those who played it.
When the season ends, it is gone.

item-tiles-season-tokyo.text: Maple Night is the Tokyo season's own set, washed in autumn colour.
You will not find it on any shelf; it is earned on the reward track, and only while the season lasts.

item-tiles-season-dubai.text: Desert Rose was made for the Dubai season, in the warm tones of sand and sunset.
Play the season, climb the reward track, and it is yours.

item-tiles-season-taipei.text: Lantern Market carries the glow of a Taipei night.
It is the Taipei season's own reward, earned at the table and never sold.

item-tiles-season-singapore.text: Garden City is the Singapore season's own set, lush and green.
It cannot be bought at any price; it is earned on the reward track, by playing the season.

item-tiles-season-hanoi.text: Lotus Lacquer was crafted for the Hanoi season, in layered lacquer and lotus gold.
It is earned on the reward track, never sold.
When it is gone, it is gone.

item-racks-rack-table.text: A perfect match is always in good taste.
These racks are cut from the very same wood as your table, with a fine brass line inlaid along the lip.

item-racks-rack-walnut.text: Club Walnut is the gentleman's choice.
Hand-oiled walnut with softly chamfered edges, green baize ledges and solid brass end caps.

item-racks-rack-rosewood.text: Run your hand along Rosewood and Brass.
Polished rosewood strung with twin brass lines, and ledges lined in oxblood leather that cradles every tile.
It feels as good as it looks.

item-racks-rack-trunk.text: Trunk Maker is inspired by the great travelling trunks: walnut and pale beech, forest-green suede and a row of hand-set brass rivets.
It makes every game feel like the start of a journey.

item-racks-rack-lacquer.text: Black Lacquer and Gold is mirror-polished, coat after coat, then edged in hand-engraved gold, with cinnabar velvet ledges.

item-racks-rack-pearl.text: Ebony and Mother of Pearl is the jeweller's rack.
Gloss ebony, inlaid with shimmering shell panels set in silver, on midnight velvet.

item-racks-rack-jade.text: Zitan and Jade is made from the rarest of woods.
Dark zitan, carved jade cartouches framed in gold, and jade cabochons crowning each cap.
A piece for a true connoisseur.

item-racks-rack-gilt.text: And this is fit for an emperor, quite literally.
Imperial Gilt is solid gilt engraved with drifting clouds, inlaid with jade, studded with rubies and lined in crimson velvet.
Nothing in the atelier is grander.

item-rooms-private-club.text: Imagine walking in here after dinner.
The Private Club is all walnut panelling, porcelain on the shelves and a lacquer pendant glowing low over the table.
Our members never want to leave.

item-rooms-tokyo.text: Tokyo Neon is my rainy-night favourite.
A tatami room tucked behind shoji screens, the city's neon shimmering through the rain outside.
Calm inside, electric beyond the glass.

item-rooms-taipei.text: Step into the Taipei Night Market.
Red lacquer columns, a moon gate, and strings of lanterns glowing over the street.
You can almost smell the food stalls.

item-rooms-dubai.text: The Dubai Majlis is hospitality made into a room.
Carved mashrabiya arches, a hand-laid zellige floor and a pierced brass lantern casting patterns at desert sunset.

item-rooms-new-york.text: Manhattan Loft is for the bold.
Exposed brick, steel-framed windows, Edison bulbs glowing above a midnight skyline.
The city never sleeps, and neither will your table.

item-rooms-shanghai.text: Shanghai in the Thirties: black lacquer, gold and a little jazz in the air, with the Bund lit up across the river.

item-rooms-modern-luxury.text: The Sky Penthouse is light itself.
White marble, walls of glass, and nothing but a calm sea far below.

item-rooms-kyoto.text: Kyoto Garden is where I go to breathe.
An open tea pavilion above a bamboo grove and a maple garden, in soft afternoon light.

item-rooms-imperial.text: The Forbidden City is the grandest hall we have.
Vermilion columns, hand-painted beams and gold at every turn.
Play here, and you are playing in the emperor's own hall.

item-rooms-hk-teahouse.text: The Hong Kong Tea House is full of life.
Teak booths, green-tiled walls, songbirds in their cages and a slow ceiling fan above a busy street.
Order a pot and settle in.

item-rooms-tokyo-janso.text: Tokyo Jansō is the real thing, a Shōwa-era parlour.
Square table lamps, rule boards on the wall, quiet tables and rain against the window.

item-rooms-al-fahidi-majlis.text: Al Fahidi Majlis takes you back in time.
Coral-stone walls, a palm-frond ceiling, sadu cushions and the scent of cardamom coffee.
Old Dubai at its most welcoming.
